The math behind choicer: hierarchical Bayesian multinomial logit

Source: vignettes/articles/hierarchical_mnl_math.Rmd
hierarchical_mnl_math.Rmd

This document describes the hierarchical Bayesian multinomial logit (HMNL) as implemented in src/hmnlogit.cpp, with shared hierarchical-Bayes infrastructure in src/hb_internal.h, sampling primitives in src/bayes_samplers.h, and the RNG core in src/rng.h. The R-side entry point is run_hmnlogit().

Notation

Symbol Description

t=1,…,Tit = 1, \dots, T_i choice situations (tasks) of respondent ii; Ti=1T_i = 1 is the cross-sectional mode
j=1,…,Jj = 1, \dots, J inside alternatives; oo denotes the implicit outside option

zjz_j PP-vector of alternative-level covariates (intercept first)
βi\beta_i respondent-level coefficients on the chain scale

b,Wb, W population mean and covariance of βi\beta_i
δj\delta_j alternative-level effect (mean utility vs the outside good)

1. Model Definition

Utilities with i.i.d. type-1 extreme value (Gumbel) shocks:

Uijt=xijt′γi+δj+εijt,Uiot=εiot,ε∼EV1,U_{ijt} = x_{ijt}'\gamma_i + \delta_j + \varepsilon_{ijt}, \qquad U_{iot} = \varepsilon_{iot}, \qquad \varepsilon \sim \text{EV1},

so the choice probabilities are the softmax against the outside anchor,

P(yit=j)=eVijt1+∑k∈CiteVikt,Vijt=xijt′γi+δj,P(y_{it} = j) = \frac{e^{V_{ijt}}}{1 + \sum_{k \in C_{it}} e^{V_{ikt}}}, \qquad V_{ijt} = x_{ijt}'\gamma_i + \delta_j,

with CitC_{it} the (possibly unbalanced) inside choice set and the 11 the outside option’s e0e^0.

Two random-effect levels, deliberately decoupled:

  • Respondent level: βi∼N(b,W)\beta_i \sim N(b, W) over the KK structural covariates only. WW is K×KK \times K — the genuine mixed-logit object. Log-normal coordinates keep the hierarchy normal on the log scale and enter utility exponentiated.
  • Alternative level (BLP-style): δj=zj′θ+ξj\delta_j = z_j'\theta + \xi_j, ξj∼N(0,σd2)\xi_j \sim N(0, \sigma_d^2). One scalar variance regardless of JJ; ξj\xi_j is the micro-Bayesian counterpart of BLP’s unobserved product quality. Partial pooling shrinks each δj\delta_j toward its characteristics-based mean, remains consistent when per-alternative data are sparse (where fixed ASC dummies suffer from incidental-parameters noise), and yields a posterior predictive for alternatives outside the estimation sample (entry counterfactuals in predict()).

Keeping the ASCs out of βi\beta_i is the scalability decision: it removes the O((K+J)3)O((K+J)^3) per-respondent Cholesky and the O(J2)O(J^2) ASC covariance block a dense specification would carry, replacing them with a length-JJ vector gathered by row index.

2. Identification

Two distinct redundancies are handled differently:

  • Scale. The EV1 shock variance is fixed (π2/6\pi^2/6), so the logit has no free scale — no normalization step is needed (contrast the HMNP).
  • Location. Adding a constant to every inside δj\delta_j cancels in the softmax unless an outside option with systematic utility 0 breaks the invariance. Version 1 requires the implicit outside option, so the δ\delta level is genuinely identified — δj\delta_j is mean utility relative to the outside good and the mean-function intercept θ0\theta_0 is the average inside-good quality vs outside. No base alternative, no sum-to-zero constraint. The level is well identified only insofar as the outside share is informative: with a tiny outside share the level posterior is diffuse (the shape — cross-alternative contrasts — remains tight).

Statistical expectations by data structure: bb and (θ,σd2,δ)(\theta, \sigma_d^2, \delta) are estimated equally well in panels and cross-sections (δ\delta is global, pooled across everyone); WW is identified in cross-sections through covariate variation and functional form but concentrates slower and leans more on its prior.

3. Priors and Joint Posterior

b∼N(b‾,A−1),W∼ℐ𝒲(ν,V),θ∼N(θ‾,Aθ−1),b \sim N(\bar b, A^{-1}), \quad W \sim \mathcal{IW}(\nu, V), \quad \theta \sim N(\bar\theta, A_\theta^{-1}),

with defaults b‾=0\bar b = 0, A=0.01IA = 0.01 I, ν=K+3\nu = K + 3, V=νIV = \nu I, θ‾=0\bar\theta = 0, Aθ=0.01IA_\theta = 0.01 I. For the alternative-effect scale, the default is a half-Cauchy: σd∼C+(0,sd)\sigma_d \sim C^+(0, s_d) via the Makalic–Schmidt inverse-gamma scale mixture

σd2∣ad∼ℐ𝒢(12,1/ad),ad∼ℐ𝒢(12,1/sd2),\sigma_d^2 \mid a_d \sim \mathcal{IG}(\tfrac12, 1/a_d), \qquad a_d \sim \mathcal{IG}(\tfrac12, 1/s_d^2),

which keeps full conjugacy while avoiding the ℐ𝒢(ϵ,ϵ)\mathcal{IG}(\epsilon, \epsilon) near-zero pathology (Gelman 2006). A plain ℐ𝒢(c0,d0)\mathcal{IG}(c_0, d_0) fallback is exposed (sd_prior$half_cauchy = FALSE).

The joint posterior over ({βi},b,W,δ,θ,σd2,ad)(\{\beta_i\}, b, W, \delta, \theta, \sigma_d^2, a_d) multiplies the logit likelihood by the two Gaussian hierarchies and the priors above.

4. The Gibbs Sampler

One systematic-scan iteration:

(0) Cache rebuild (work-shared over respondents, fixed order): linear predictors vv, level-form task denominators Dt=1+∑insideevD_t = 1 + \sum_{\text{inside}} e^v, per-task and per-respondent log-likelihoods. Rebuilt every iteration — needed anyway because the β\beta phase changes them, and it bounds incremental floating-point drift to a single sweep.

(a) βi\beta_i — adaptive RW-Metropolis (work-shared over respondents). Proposal β*=βi+siL−Tz\beta^* = \beta_i + s_i L^{-T} z with LL′=Hi+W−1LL' = H_i + W^{-1}, where HiH_i is the respondent information at the pooled MNL MLE,

Hi=∑t(∑jpjtxjtxjt′−x‾tx‾t′),x‾t=∑jpjtxjt,H_i = \sum_{t} \Big( \sum_j p_{jt} x_{jt} x_{jt}' - \bar x_t \bar x_t' \Big), \qquad \bar x_t = \sum_j p_{jt} x_{jt},

computed once at startup with probabilities at (γ̂pooled,δinit)(\hat\gamma_{\text{pooled}}, \delta_{\text{init}}), the outside option contributing probability mass at x=0x = 0. For log-normal coordinates HiH_i is Jacobian-adjusted to the chain scale (row and column kk scaled by γ̂k\hat\gamma_k). Acceptance uses one fresh likelihood pass over the respondent’s own rows (non-finite ⇒\Rightarrow auto-reject, which guards eβe^\beta overflow) plus the prior quadratic forms 12[(βi−b)′W−1(βi−b)−(β*−b)′W−1(β*−b)]\tfrac12[(\beta_i - b)'W^{-1}(\beta_i - b) - (\beta^* - b)'W^{-1}(\beta^* - b)]. log⁡si\log s_i is Robbins–Monro-adapted toward 0.234 during burn-in with gain (r+1)−0.6(r+1)^{-0.6}, clamped to [log⁡0.01,log⁡10][\log 0.01, \log 10], and frozen at the end of burn-in.

(b) δj\delta_j — strictly serial RW-Metropolis sweep (master thread). The δj\delta_j full conditionals are coupled through the shared softmax denominators — every task containing several inside alternatives ties their δ\delta’s together — so a work-shared (synchronous) update across jj would not leave the posterior invariant. Each update must see the latest δ\delta and caches. The sweep stays cheap: for a proposal δj*=δj+sδjz\delta_j^* = \delta_j + s_{\delta j} z, the log-likelihood change over the tasks containing jj is

Δℓ=∑t∋j[(δj*−δj)𝟙{yt=j}−log⁡(Dt−ejt+ejt*)+log⁡Dt]\Delta \ell = \sum_{t \ni j} \Big[ (\delta_j^* - \delta_j)\, \mathbb{1}\{y_t = j\} - \log(D_t - e_{jt} + e^*_{jt}) + \log D_t \Big]

from the cached DtD_t and ejt=evjte_{jt} = e^{v_{jt}} — O(1)O(1) per affected task; an accepted move updates the caches in place so δj+1\delta_{j+1} sees the latest state. (Dt≥1D_t \ge 1 always because of the outside term, so log⁡Dt\log D_t is safe.) The Gaussian prior is N(zj′θ,σd2)N(z_j'\theta, \sigma_d^2); the scalar acceptance target is 0.44. Contrast the HMNP, whose δj\delta_j conditionals are conditionally independent given the augmented utilities and are drawn in parallel — the asymmetry is documented in src/hb_internal.h.

(c) Hierarchy (master thread, conjugate):

  • b∣β,W∼N((A+NW−1)−1(Ab‾+W−1∑iβi),(A+NW−1)−1)b \mid \beta, W \sim N\big((A + N W^{-1})^{-1}(A\bar b + W^{-1}\sum_i \beta_i),\; (A + N W^{-1})^{-1}\big)
  • W∣β,b∼ℐ𝒲(ν+N,V+∑i(βi−b)(βi−b)′)W \mid \beta, b \sim \mathcal{IW}\big(\nu + N,\; V + \sum_i (\beta_i - b)(\beta_i - b)'\big)
  • θ∣δ,σd2∼N((Aθ+Z′Z/σd2)−1(Aθθ‾+Z′δ/σd2),⋅)\theta \mid \delta, \sigma_d^2 \sim N\big((A_\theta + Z'Z/\sigma_d^2)^{-1}(A_\theta\bar\theta + Z'\delta/\sigma_d^2),\; \cdot\big)
  • σd2∣δ,θ,ad∼ℐ𝒢(12+J2,1/ad+12∑jξj2)\sigma_d^2 \mid \delta, \theta, a_d \sim \mathcal{IG}(\tfrac12 + \tfrac J2,\; 1/a_d + \tfrac12\sum_j \xi_j^2) and ad∣σd2∼ℐ𝒢(1,1/sd2+1/σd2)a_d \mid \sigma_d^2 \sim \mathcal{IG}(1,\; 1/s_d^2 + 1/\sigma_d^2) (the half-Cauchy mixture), with ξ=δ−Zθ\xi = \delta - Z\theta.

Initialization. βi\beta_i start at the pooled MNL MLE over the structural covariates (computed through the existing frequentist kernel with the implicit outside option; log-normal coordinates transformed with a warn-and-clamp log⁡(max⁡(γ̂k,0.05))\log(\max(\hat\gamma_k, 0.05))); δ\delta at shrunk log choice-share contrasts log⁡((nj+12)/(no+12))\log\big((n_j + \tfrac12)/(n_o + \tfrac12)\big); θ\theta at the OLS regression of δinit\delta_{\text{init}} on ZZ.

5. Sampling Primitives

Worker threads may never call BLAS/LAPACK or the R API (see §7), so the per-respondent proposal uses the hand-rolled dense Cholesky, triangular solves, and precision-parameterized MVN draw in src/hb_internal.h (hb_chol_lower, hb_back_solve, hb_mvn_precision_draw), all with caller-owned scratch to avoid hot-loop allocation. Master-side conjugate draws use draw_b_conditional, draw_W_conditional (via riwishart_nothrow), draw_theta_conditional, and draw_sigma_d2_conditional. Inverse-gamma draws are scale / rgamma(shape) from the Xoshiro256++ stream — never R’s RNG.

6. Post-Processing and Reported Quantities

run_hmnlogit() reports the posterior of bb (coefficients / SE / vcov from the draws), the θ\theta and σd2\sigma_d^2 summaries, the posterior-mean WW, the quality ladder — per-alternative posteriors of δj\delta_j and ξj=δj−zj′θ\xi_j = \delta_j - z_j'\theta — accumulated online (Welford), the per-respondent βi\beta_i summaries per keep_beta_i, acceptance diagnostics, and the split-R̂\widehat R table over chains (rhat()). Post-estimation methods (predict, wtp, logsum, consumer_surplus, elasticities, diversion_ratios, ppc_shares) integrate over the posterior draws; new alternatives in predict(newdata=) receive a posterior-predictive δnew∼N(znew′θr,σd,r2)\delta_{\text{new}} \sim N(z_{\text{new}}'\theta_r, \sigma_{d,r}^2) per draw.

Endogeneity. If a price-like covariate is correlated with ξj\xi_j, the estimates are exogenous only conditional on ZZ. The preps accept a user-supplied first-stage residual (cf_residual_col, Petrin–Train 2010) that enters XX as an ordinary covariate; the first stage is not run by the package and posterior uncertainty does not propagate first-stage error (joint Bayesian IV is roadmapped).

7. Implementation Details

The kernel follows the src/mnprobit.cpp engine contract:

  • One persistent OpenMP parallel region for the whole chain; the β\beta phase and cache rebuild are work-shared over respondents (each task belongs to exactly one respondent, so all cache slots are respondent-owned); the serial δ\delta sweep, hierarchy draws, recording, trace, and the interrupt poll run in a master block between barriers.
  • RNG partition per iteration rr via make_stream(seed, r, tag): tag ii = respondent ii’s MH work; tag 2N+j2N + j = δj\delta_j; tags 2N+J+{0,1,2,3}2N + J + \{0,1,2,3\} = b,W,θ,σd2b, W, \theta, \sigma_d^2. The master block is based at 2N+J2N + J (not 3N3N), so the partition is collision-free for any JJ, including J>NJ > N.
  • Bitwise thread invariance: per-(iteration, unit) RNG streams, fixed-order accumulation of every cross-respondent quantity on the master thread, and the master-only δ\delta sweep make the draws bitwise independent of the thread count (tested 1-vs-4 threads, including the J>NJ > N regime).
  • Abort protocol: worker-side failures set an abort code in a critical section; every thread re-checks after barriers and exits together; Rcpp::stop fires after the region. User interrupts are polled every 100 iterations on the master thread.
